topics.title: Welcome to the Agency
topics.objective: Learn why you are here and how to move through HQ.
topics.controlIntro: Welcome, recruit. I am CONTROL. This academy is orientation only — no grades, no SCR, and no live mission doors.
topics.explanation: API Spy trains you to read documentation and build HTTP requests inside fictional escape-room missions. You play as a field agent. Training rooms teach concepts safely. Independent missions on the Operations Board are separate assessed practice rooms.

workedExample.title: Movement briefing
workedExample.notes: Use WASD or arrow keys to walk. Stand near a yellow terminal and press E to open the API editor. Hearts never drop for API mistakes.
workedExample.body: Controls: WASD / Arrows · Interact: E · API mistakes: no heart loss

options.label: It grades your first independent mission for RCA.
It is ungraded orientation before independent missions.

interaction.successFeedback: Correct. Module 0 is orientation. Graded first attempts begin only on independent Module 1 missions.
interaction.failureFeedback: Not quite. Module 0 never grades RCA or unlocks live mission doors. Review the briefing and try again.

topics.completionMessage: Topic complete. You understand training versus independent operations.

topics.title: Understanding APIs
topics.objective: See how a client request becomes a server response.
topics.controlIntro: An API is a contract: you send a structured request, the server replies with a status and body. In API Spy every exchange is fictional.
topics.explanation: Think of an intelligence records desk. Your terminal asks for a file. The desk replies with a code (such as 200) and JSON. Nothing you type leaves this training network.

workedExample.title: Fictional records exchange
workedExample.notes: Request GET /api/training/records/demo → Response 200 with a sample agent card.

interaction.prompt: Press Send on the demo request. Confirm you can read the simulated 200 response.
interaction.successFeedback: Good. You read a simulated response. Live missions use different paths.
interaction.failureFeedback: Send the demo request and read the status before continuing.

topics.completionMessage: Topic complete. You can follow a request → response loop.

topics.title: HTTP Methods
topics.objective: Choose the right method for a fictional objective.
topics.controlIntro: Methods name the action. GET reads. POST creates. PUT replaces. PATCH updates part. DELETE removes. Module 1 focuses on GET first.
topics.explanation: Each method has a job. Escaping a locked door usually means retrieving status with GET. Creating a new dossier would use POST. API Spy Module 1 practice rooms emphasize GET.

workedExample.title: Separate fictional examples
workedExample.body: GET reads · POST creates · PUT replaces · PATCH patches · DELETE removes

interaction.prompt: You must retrieve an existing door status without changing it. Which method fits?
interaction.successFeedback: Correct. GET retrieves a representation without creating or deleting the resource.
interaction.failureFeedback: Retrieve means read. Choose GET, then revisit the method chart if needed.

topics.completionMessage: Topic complete. You can match objectives to HTTP methods.

topics.title: Endpoints and Resources
topics.objective: Recognize resource paths in fictional URLs.
topics.controlIntro: An endpoint is the path after the host — the resource you are talking to. Spelling matters.
topics.explanation: A path like /api/training/lockers/academy names a locker resource. Collections often look like /api/items and one item like /api/items/alpha. Mission doors use different paths than training lockers.

workedExample.title: URL structure
workedExample.body: /api/{collection}/{id} identifies one resource in a collection.

interaction.prompt: Which path correctly targets the academy training locker?
interaction.successFeedback: Correct. Training lockers live under /api/training/…. Door Alpha is a graded Module 1 path — leave it for later.
interaction.failureFeedback: Avoid mission door paths here. Pick the /api/training/lockers/academy endpoint.

topics.completionMessage: Topic complete. You can tell training endpoints from mission endpoints.

topics.title: Parameters and Responses
topics.objective: Separate path params, query params, and common status codes.
topics.controlIntro: Path parameters sit inside the path. Query parameters follow ?. Status codes tell you how the server answered.
topics.explanation: Path example: /api/training/crates/{crateId} → /api/training/crates/crate-42. Query example: /api/training/signals?channel=green. Statuses: 200 OK, 201 Created, 400 Bad Request, 401 Unauthorized, 404 Not Found, 500 Server Error.

workedExample.title: Statuses to remember
workedExample.notes: 200 success · 201 created · 400 client mistake · 401 auth · 404 missing · 500 server fault
workedExample.body: Wrong path or params often produce 400-style simulated errors in API Spy.

interaction.successFeedback: Correct. It replaces {crateId} inside the path. Query parameters would appear after ?.
interaction.failureFeedback: Values inside the path are path parameters. Query parameters appear after ?.

topics.completionMessage: Topic complete. You can separate parameters and read status codes.

topics.title: Terminal Field Training
topics.objective: Walk to a training terminal and submit a fictional GET.
topics.controlIntro: Enter the safe training room. Walk to the terminal, press E, and retrieve /api/training/lockers/academy. Unlimited retries. No graded first attempt.
topics.explanation: This room has no enemies. Completing the terminal interaction finishes Module 0. The contract uses a training path — never Door Alpha.

interaction.prompt: Complete the training terminal request successfully.
interaction.successFeedback: Training terminal cleared. Orientation can be marked complete.
interaction.failureFeedback: Check method and path against the training documentation, then retry.

topics.completionMessage: Field training complete. Report back to the Operations Board when ready.
